name: glowing-effect

frames.best_why: A bright arc runs along the top-right card's outline while the other cards stay dark.

tagline: A bright arc of light runs along the card border nearest your cursor.
summary: A border glow that tracks the pointer: a card outline lights up with a short arc on the side facing the cursor and fades when the pointer moves away.
appearance: Five near-black cards in an uneven grid, each with a small icon in a bordered square, a bold white heading and grey supporting text. The hovered card's thin border shows a bright segment that fades into the rest of the outline.
behaviour: As the pointer moves, a bright wedge of gradient travels around the border of the nearby card to face it, easing into place; leaving fades it back to a plain outline. The card itself never moves.
demo_content: Cards headed 'Do things the right way', 'The best AI code editor ever.' and similar placeholder lines about the product.
search_phrases: glowing border that follows the mouse
card outline lights up on hover
neon edge on a feature card
gradient outline that tracks the cursor
use_when: A grid of feature or pricing cards needs a subtle hover cue without changing the card layout.
avoid_when: The effect is decorative and pointer-only, so touch and keyboard users never see it.
customise: Tune blur, proximity, spread, inactiveZone, border width, movement duration, variant and a disabled flag; the gradient palette itself is fixed in the source.
weight_why: One CSS mask with a short animation per pointer move, idle otherwise.

a11y.note: The glow is pointer-only, so keyboard and touch users get no equivalent cue from this component.

issues: The demo copy is obvious filler, which weakens how the effect reads in a gallery.
At rest every card is a plain flat outline, so the effect can look like nothing at all.
polish_why: The border light is tasteful and smooth; placeholder copy and a faint rest state let it down.
title: Glowing Effect
